Preemption_mode.description: Preemption mode selection; Set configUSE_PREEMPTION to 1 to use pre-emptive scheduling.  Set configUSE_PREEMPTION to 0 to use co-operative scheduling.

Use_time_slicing.title: Use Time Slicing
Use_time_slicing.description: Set configUSE_TIME_SLICING to 1 to have the scheduler switch between Ready state tasks of equal priority on every tick interrupt.  Set configUSE_TIME_SLICING to 0 to prevent the scheduler switching between Ready state tasks just because there was a tick interrupt.

Minimum_stack_size.title: Minimum stack size
Minimum_stack_size.description:
Set the minimum stack size. Sets the size of the stack allocated to the idle task. The value is specified in words (here, of 32 bits), not bytes.
Warning: The value chosen by the user should take into account the number of threads, the total heap size and the system stack size. If the totality of used stack size is higher than the total heap size, FreeRTOS will not be able to create and manage the tasks.
For information: max value = configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE/4 (when allocation is dynamic) 
 max value = MCU ram size/4 (when allocation is static)

Minimum_secure_stack_size.title: Minimum secure stack size
Minimum_secure_stack_size.description: Stack for idle task Secure side context in words.

Max_priorities.title: Maximum Task Priorities
Max_priorities.description: configMAX_PRIORITIES Sets the number of available task priorities.  Tasks can be assigned priorities of 0 to (configMAX_PRIORITIES - 1).  Zero is the lowest priority.

Mutexes.title: Mutexes
Mutexes.description: Set to 1 to include mutexe functionality in the build, or 0 to omit mutex functionality from the build.

Recursive_Mutexes.title: Recursive Mutexes
Recursive_Mutexes.description: Set to 1 to include reccursive mutexe functionality in the build, or 0 to omit recursive mutex functionality from the build.

actions.message: Set Mutexes to 1 in the Kernel panel to use Recursive Mutexes.

Counting_semaphore.title: Counting Semaphores
Counting_semaphore.description: Set to 1 to include counting semaphore functionality in the build, or 0 to omit counting semaphore functionality from the build.

Notification.title: Notifications
Notification.description: Set to 1 to include notification functionality in the build, or 0 to omit notification functionality from the build.

actions.message: Notifications should be enabled when Stream Buffers is set to 1 in the Kernel panel.

Queue.title: Queue Sets
Queue.description: Set to 1 to include Queue set functionality in the build, or 0 to omit Queue set functionality from the build.

Queue_size.title: Queue size
Queue_size.description:
The maximum queue size to be used when queue object is created.
Set configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE to the maximum number of queues and semaphores that can be referenced from the queue registry.  Only required when using a kernel aware debugger.

Event_groups.title: Event Groups
Event_groups.description: Set configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS to 1 to include event group functionality in the build. Set to 0 to exclude event group functionality from the build. The FreeRTOS/source/event_groups.c source file must be included in the build if configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS is set to 1. Defaults to 1 if left undefined.

Stream_buffers.title: Stream Buffers
Stream_buffers.description: Set configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS to 1 to include stream buffer functionality in the build. Set to 0 to exclude event group functionality from the build. The FreeRTOS/source/stream_buffer.c source file must be included in the build if configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS is set to 1. Defaults to 1 if left undefined.

Software_Timer.title: Software timer
Software_Timer.description: Set to 1 to include Software timer functionality in the build, or 0 to omit Software timer functionality from the build.

Timer_task_priority_level.title: Timer task priority level
Timer_task_priority_level.description:
Sets the priority of the software timer service/daemon task.
Note:
Available as configUse_TIMERS is enabled.

actions.message: Should be less than or equal to "Maximum Task Priorities" - 1U.

Timer_queue_length.title: Timer queue length
Timer_queue_length.description:
Sets the length of the software timer command queue.
Note: Available as configUse_TIMERS is enabled.

Timer_stack_size.title: Timer stack size
Timer_stack_size.description:
Sets the size of the stack (in words, not bytes) allocated to the timer service task.
Note: Available as configUse_TIMERS is enabled (dynamic allocation used for the timer task).

Tickeless_mode.title: Tickeless mode
Tickeless_mode.description:
By setting the configUSE_TICKLESS_IDLE, the idle task suppresses ticks and the processor stays in a low power mode for as long as possible.
- When set to 1 (Built in functionality enabled), two macros, configPRE_SLEEP_PROCESSING and configPOST_SLEEP_PROCESSING are generated in FreeRTOSConfig.h, and two empty functions, PreSleepProcessing and PostSleepProcessing generated in freertos.c (to be completed with user code).
- When set to 2 (User defined functionality enabled), one empty function, vPortSuppressTicksAndSleep is generated in freertos.c (to be completed with user code).

MPU_mode.title: MPU mode
MPU_mode.description: Set configENABLE_MPU to 1 to enable the Memory Protection Unit (MPU), or 0 to leave the Memory Protection Unit disabled.

FPU_mode.title: FPU mode
FPU_mode.description: Set configENABLE_FPU to 1 to enable the Floating Point Unit (FPU) or 0 to leave the Floating Point Unit disabled.

Idle_task_mode.description: Set configIDLE_SHOULD_YIELD to 1 to have the Idle task yield to an application task if there is an Idle priority (priority 0) application task that can run.  Set to 0 to have the Idle task use all of its timeslice.  Default to 1 if left undefined.

Application_task_tag.description:
USE_APPLICATION_TASK_TAG must be defined as 1 for the vTaskSetApplicationTaskTag function to be available.
 This function is intended for advanced users only.
 A 'tag' value can be assigned to each task. This value is for the use of the application only.
- The RTOS kernel itself does not make use of it in any way.
- The FreeRTOS trace macros documentation page provides a good example of how an application might make use of this feature.

Port_optimized_task_selection.description:
Some FreeRTOS ports have two methods of selecting the next task to execute - a generic method, and a method that is specific to that port.
The Generic method: 
- Is used when configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION is set to 0, or when a port specific method is not implemented.
- Can be used with all FreeRTOS ports.
- Is completely written in C, making it less efficient than a port specific method.
- Does not impose a limit on the maximum number of available priorities.
A port specific method:
- Is not available for all ports.
- Is used when configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION is set to 1.
- Relies on one or More architecture specific assembly instructions (typically a Count Leading Zeros [CLZ] of equivalent instruction) so can only be used with the architecture for which it was specifically written.
- Is more efficient than the generic method.
- Typically imposes a limit of 32 on the maximum number of available priorities.

actions.message: #error configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION can only be set to 1 when configMAX_PRIORITIES is less than or equal to 32.  It is very rare that a system requires more than 10 to 15 different priorities as tasks that share a priority will time slice.

Backward_compatibility.description: Set configENABLE_BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY to 1 to map function names and datatypes from old version of FreeRTOS to their latest equivalent.

Task_name_maximum_length.title: Task name maximum length
Task_name_maximum_length.description: Sets the maximum number of characters that can be used for the name of a task. The NULL terminator is included in the count of characters.

Number_of_thread_local_storage_pointers.title: Number of Thread Local Storage Pointers
Number_of_thread_local_storage_pointers.description: Specifies the number of thread-local storage pointers available for each task.

Provide_static_memory.title: Provide Static Memory by Kernel
Provide_static_memory.description: Defines the kernel provided implementation of vApplicationGetIdleTaskMemory() and vApplicationGetTimerTaskMemory() to provide the memory that is used by the Idle task and Timer task respectively. The application can provide it's own implementation of vApplicationGetIdleTaskMemory() and vApplicationGetTimerTaskMemory() by setting configKERNEL_PROVIDED_STATIC_MEMORY to 0 or leaving it undefined.

USE_TRACE_FACILITY.title: USE_TRACE_FACILITY
USE_TRACE_FACILITY.description: Set to 1 (Enabled) if you wish to include additional structure members and functions to assist with execution visualization and tracing.

CPU_frequency.title: CPU frequency in Hz
CPU_frequency.description: CPU frequency in Hz; This must be set to the frequency of the clock that drives the peripheral used to generate the kernels periodic tick interrupt. This is very often, but not always, equal to the main system clock frequency.

Systick_frequency.title: Systick frequency in Hz
Systick_frequency.description:
Optional parameter for ARM Cortex-M ports only.
By default ARM Cortex-M ports generate the RTOS tick interrupt from the Cortex-M SysTick timer.
Most Cortex-M MCUs run the SysTick timer at the same frequency as the MCU itself, when that is the case 
configSYSTICK_CLOCK_HZ  is not needed and should be left undefined.
If the SysTick timer is clocked at a different frequency to the MCU core then set  configCPU_CLOCK_HZ to the MCU clock frequency, as normal, and  configSYSTICK_CLOCK_HZ to the SysTick clock frequency.

RTOS_Tick_frequency.title: RTOS Tick frequency
RTOS_Tick_frequency.description:
The frequency of the RTOS tick interrupt.
The tick interrupt is used to measure time. Therefore a higher tick frequency means time can be measured to a higher resolution. However, a high tick frequency also means that the RTOS kernel will use more CPU time so be less efficient. The RTOS demo applications all use a tick rate of 1000Hz. This is used to test the RTOS kernel and is higher than would normally be required.

LIBRARY_LOWEST_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY.title: Library Lowest Interrupt Priority
LIBRARY_LOWEST_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY.description: The lowest interrupt priority that can be used in a call to a set priority function.

LIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY.title: Library Max Syscall Interrupt Priority
LIBRARY_MAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY.description:
The highest interrupt priority that can be used by any interrupt service routine that makes calls to interrupt safe FreeRTOS API functions.
DO NOT CALL INTERRUPT SAFE FREERTOS API FUNCTIONS FROM ANY INTERRUPT THAT HAS A HIGHER PRIORITY THAN THIS! (higher priorities are lower numeric values).

Check_handler.title: Check Handler installation
Check_handler.description: Set configCHECK_HANDLER_INSTALLATION to 1 to enable additional asserts to verify that the application has correctly installed FreeRTOS interrupt handlers.

actions.message: Memory allocation Type must be set to Dynamic or Dynamic/Static when a heap is selected.

Total_Heap_size.title: Total Heap size
Total_Heap_size.description:
The total amount of RAM available in the FreeRTOS heap.
This value will only be used if configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION is set to 1 and the application makes use of one of the sample memory allocation schemes provided in the FreeRTOS source code download.

Application_allocated_heap.title: Application Allocated Heap
Application_allocated_heap.description: Set configAPPLICATION_ALLOCATED_HEAP to 1 to have the application allocate the array used as the FreeRTOS heap.  Set to 0 to have the linker allocate the array used as the FreeRTOS heap. Defaults to 0 if left undefined.

Stack_allocation_from_separate_heap.title: Stack Allocation From Separate Heap
Stack_allocation_from_separate_heap.description: Set configSTACK_ALLOCATION_FROM_SEPARATE_HEAP to 1 to have task stacks allocated from somewhere other than the FreeRTOS heap. This is useful if you want to ensure stacks are held in fast memory. Set to 0 to have task stacks come from the standard FreeRTOS heap. The application writer must provide implementations for pvPortMallocStack() and vPortFreeStack() if set to 1. Defaults to 0 if left undefined.

Heap_clear_memory_on_free.title: Clear Memory On Free
Heap_clear_memory_on_free.description: When set to 1, the memory freed using vPortFree() is automatically cleared to zero.

Use_mini_list_item.title: Use Mini List Item
Use_mini_list_item.description: When configUSE_MINI_LIST_ITEM is set to 0, MiniListItem_t and ListItem_t are both the same. When configUSE_MINI_LIST_ITEM is set to 1, MiniListItem_t contains 3 fewer fields than ListItem_t which saves some RAM at the cost of violating strict aliasing rules which some compilers depend on for optimization. Defaults to 1 if left undefined.

Enable_heap_protector.title: Enable Heap Protector
Enable_heap_protector.description: Set configENABLE_HEAP_PROTECTOR to 1 to enable bounds checking and obfuscation to internal heap block pointers in heap_4.c and heap_5.c to help catch pointer corruptions. Defaults to 0 if left undefined.

Advanced_API_selector.title: Advanced API Selector
Advanced_API_selector.description: Set the following configUSE_* constants to 1 to include the named feature in the build, or 0 to exclude the named feature from the build.

vTaskPrioritySet.title: vTaskPrioritySet
vTaskPrioritySet.description:
It is one of the macros allowing those components of the real time kernel not utilized by your application to be excluded from your build.
- This ensures the RTOS does not use any more ROM or RAM than necessary for your particular embedded application. 
To include the vTaskPrioritySet() API function, set vTaskPrioritySet to 1 (Enabled) and to exclude it from your build, set vTaskPrioritySet to 0 (Disabled).

xQueueGetMutexHolder.title: xQueueGetMutexHolder
xQueueGetMutexHolder.description: Configuration constant introduced in FreeRTOS v7.2.0 that is used as the default value of xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder (if it is not explicitly set).

xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder.title: xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder
xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder.description:

xEventGroupSetBitFromISR.title: xEventGroupSetBitFromISR
xEventGroupSetBitFromISR.description:
Set bits (flags) within an RTOS event group. A version of xEventGroupSetBits() that can be called from an interrupt service routine (ISR).
- Note: INCLUDE_xTimerPendFunctionCall must be set to 1 to make the xEventGroupSetBitFromISR() function available.
- Dependency: Must be set to 0 (Disabled) when xTimerPendFunctionCall = 0 (Disabled).

xTimerPendFunctionCall.title: xTimerPendFunctionCall

actions.message: The Software Timer must be set to 1 in the Kernel panel to enable the xTimerPendFunctionCall() function.

xTimerPendFunctionCall.description:
Used to pend the execution of a function to the RTOS daemon task (the timer service task, hence this function is pre-fixed with 'Timer').
Note: configUSE_TIMERS must be set to 1 to make the xTimerPendFunctionCall() function available.

USE_IDLE_HOOK.title: USE_IDLE_HOOK
USE_IDLE_HOOK.description:
The idle task hook function is a hook (or callback) function that, if defined and configured, will be called by the idle task on each iteration of its implementation.
- if USE_IDLE_HOOK is set to 1 (Enabled) then the application must define an idle task hook function: void vApplicationIdleHook(void).
- if USE_IDLE_HOOK is set to 0 (Disabled) then the idle task hook function will not be called, even if one is defined.
Note: When set to 1, an empty function is generated in the app_freertos.c file (to be completed by the user).

USE_TICK_HOOK.title: USE_TICK_HOOK
USE_TICK_HOOK.description:
The tick hook function is a hook (or callback) function that, if defined and configured, will be called during each tick interrupt.
- if USE_TICK_HOOK is set to 1 (Enabled) then the application must define a tick hook function; void vApplicationTickHook(void).
- if USE_TICK_HOOK is set to 0 (Disabled) then the tick hook function will not be called, even if one is defined.
Note: When set to 1, an empty function is generated in the freertos.c file (to be completed by the user).

CHEK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW.title: CHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW
CHEK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW.description:
FreeRTOS provides two optional mechanisms that can be used to assist in stack overflow detection and debugging.
- when CHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW is set to 1 (option1), one mechanism is used.
- when CHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW is set to 2 (option2), both mechanisms are used.
If CHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW is not set to 0 (Disabled), the application must provide a stack overflow hook (or callback) function: void vApplicationStackOverflowHook( xTaskHandle xTask, signed char *pcTaskName );
The kernel will call that stack overflow hook whenever a stack overflow is detected.
Note: When set to 1 or 2, a function with an empty body is generated in the freertos.c file (to be completed by the user).

USE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK.title: USE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK
USE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK.description:
The malloc() failed hook function is a hook (or callback) function that, if defined and configured, will be called if pvPortMalloc() ever returns NULL.
- NULL will be returned only if there is insufficient FreeRTOS heap memory remaining for the requested allocation to succeed.
- If USE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK is set to 1 (Enabled) then the application must define a malloc() failed hook function: void vApplicationMallocFailedHook(void).
- If USE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK is set to 0 (Disabled) then the malloc() failed hook function will not be called, even if one is defined.
Note: when set to 1, an empty function is generated in the freertos.c file (to be completed by the user).

USE_DAEMON_TASK_STARTUP_HOOK.title: USE_DAEMON_TASK_STARTUP_HOOK
USE_DAEMON_TASK_STARTUP_HOOK.description:
If USE_TIMERS and USE_DAEMON_TASK_STARTUP_HOOK are both set to 1 (Enabled) then the application must define an hook function: void vApplicationDaemonTaskStartupHook(void).
Note:
- When set to 1, an empty function is generated in the freertos.c file (to be completed by the user).
- Added since support of FreeRTOS v9.

configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK.title: USE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK.description: Set configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK to 1 to have send and receive completed callbacks for each instance of a stream buffer or message buffer. When the option is set to 1, APIs xStreamBufferCreateWithCallback() and xStreamBufferCreateStaticWithCallback() (and likewise APIs for message buffer) can be used to create a stream buffer or message buffer instance with application provided callbacks. Defaults to 0 if left undefined.

GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS.title: GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS
GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS.description:
FreeRTOS can be configured to collect task run time statistics.
The vTaskGetRunTimeStats() API function formats the collected run time statistics into a human readable table.
GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS must be set to 1 (Enabled) for vTaskGetRunTimeStats() to be available.
Note: when set to 1, two empty functions are generated in the app_freertos.c file (to be completed by the user).

USE_STATS_FORMATTING_FUNCTIONS.title: USE_STATS_FORMATTING_FUNCTIONS
USE_STATS_FORMATTING_FUNCTIONS.description:
Set USE_TRACE_FACILITY and USE_STATS_FORMATTING_FUNCTIONS to 1 (Enabled) to include the vTaskList() and vTaskGetRunTimeStats() functions in the build.
Setting either to 0 (Disabled) will omit vTaskList() and vTaskGetRunTimeStates() from the build.

actions.message: configUSE_STATS_FORMATTING_FUNCTIONS cannot be used without enabling Dynamic or Dynamic/Static allocation memory type in the Memory Management panel.

Enable_TRUSTZONE.title: Enable TRUSTZONE
Enable_TRUSTZONE.description: Set configENABLE_TRUSTZONE to 1 when running FreeRTOS on the non-secure side to enable the TrustZone support in FreeRTOS ARMv8-M ports which allows the non-secure FreeRTOS tasks to call the (non-secure callable) functions exported from secure side.

RUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY.title: Run FreeRTOS Secure Only
RUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY.description: If the application writer does not want to use TrustZone, but the hardware does not support disabling TrustZone then the entire application (including the FreeRTOS scheduler) can run on the secure side without ever branching to the non-secure side. To do that, in addition to setting configENABLE_TRUSTZONE to 0, also set configRUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY to 1.

Enable_PAC.title: Enable PAC
Enable_PAC.description: Set configENABLE_PAC to 1 to enable Pointer Authentication Security Feature PAC and 0 to disable it. It is used only in ARMv8.1-M ports.

Enable_BTI.title: Enable BTI
Enable_BTI.description: Set configENABLE_BTI to 1 to enable Branch Target Identification Security Feature BTI and 0 to disable it. It is used only in ARMv8.1-M ports.

Enable_MVE.title: Enable MVE
Enable_MVE.description: Set configENABLE_MVE to 1 to enable the M-Profile Vector Extension (MVE) support, or 0 to leave the MVE support disabled. This option is only applicable to Cortex-M55 and Cortex-M85 ports as M-Profile Vector Extension (MVE) is available only on these architectures. configENABLE_MVE must be left undefined, or defined to 0 for the Cortex-M23,Cortex-M33 and Cortex-M35P ports.

actions.message: Should be less than or equal to "Maximum Task Priorities" - 1U.

Parameter.title: Parameter
Parameter.description: A value that is passed as the paramater to the created task. If pvParameters is set to the address of a variable then the variable must still exist when the created task executes so it is not valid to pass the address of a stack variable.

ControlBlockName.title: Control block name
ControlBlockName.description: Structure that will hold the TCB of the task being created.

Max_count.title: Max Counter
Max_count.description: The maximum count value that can be reached. When the semaphore reaches this value it can no longer be 'given'.

Initial_count.title: Initial Counter
Initial_count.description: The count value assigned to the semaphore when it is created.

Buffer_size.title: Buffer size
Buffer_size.description: The maximum number of items the queue can hold at any one time.

Queue_item_size.title: Queue item size
Queue_item_size.description: The size, in bytes, required to hold each item in the queue. Items are queued by copy, not by reference, so this is the number of bytes that will be copied for each queued  Each item in the queue must be the same size.
